full_judgment:
9. Mr Moudud Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing for the pre-emptee-petitioner after placing the impugned order as well as the judgment of the Mal Court below submits that the impugned order is not at all a proper judgment of reversal inasmuch the Court of appeal below without adverting the findings of the trial Court below abruptly arrived at a finding that the trial Court below committed illegality in holding that the pre-emptor is not a co-sharer to the case jote. Mr Moudud Ahmed further upon referring the evidence of OPWs submits that the pre-emptee purchaser himself was examined as OPW-1, who in his evidence categorically stated that the pre-emptor is not a co-sharer to the case land and the pre-emptee purchaser is a co-sharer to the case jote and he has more land surrounding the case land but the Court of appeal below as last Court of fact without considering the evidence of OPWs and without adverting the material finding of the trial Court below most illegally set-aside the judgment of the trial Court below which resulted in the failure of justice. Finally, Mr Moudud Ahmed submits that as per mutation Khatian No.2962 the co-sharer ship of the pre-emptor-opposite party No.1 has been ceased and since the pre-emptor lost his co-sharer ship by separating his joma through Mutation Case No.7396 of 2011 he cannot apply for pre-emption. 10. Drawing support of his submission, the learned Advocate has relied on a decision reported in 55 DLR 214. 

 23. Another bane of contention raised in this revision that the impugned judgment is not a proper judgment of reversal.
